data.name: Tubular Rift
data.detailed_description:
Tubular Rift: In the far-flung future race on different planets. In old tubes meant to hit the rift. The rift being another dimension parallel to our own. The rewards are great! The consequences are even greater! As a racer in this vast universe, you are here to win. Race across the galaxy, in order to take the title of Rift Champion. Race against the Universe most advance A.I. racers. Prove to the Universe that the human mind and reflexes are still better than A.I. Race against other Humans who hungry to win.

Excerpt:
1: The game has full controller support for the Xbox 360 in game. Though you must use the mouse on the launcher in order to start the game.
2: MultiPlayer coming soon!
3: Split Screen Coming soon!

reviews.review:
[quote][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/32732116-IndieGems/]Follow our curator page: [b]IndieGems[/b] if you like and want to see more reviews like this one.[/url][/quote]

[h1]The Game[/h1]
[i]Tubular Rift[/i] is advertised as an action racing title still in Early Access with VR support. The game focuses on these loops that are supposedly a parallel dimension where you travel. The game falls apart at multiple levels and does not seem ready for public consumption at this time.

[h1]Gameplay and My Experience[/h1]
You select one of many (I didn't count how many) racers/vehicles, choose from three difficulty settings, how many enemy bots, how many laps, and one of five venues, and off you are to a roller coaster ride. I wanted to see the different designs of the vehicles before starting, but they rotate so slowly and there is no way to look at them except for allow the thing to slowly turn. See beginning of my video below. I could not patiently wait any longer.

I call it a roller coaster because that is what it feels like. The tubes severely limit your movement and moving around only allows you to move in a circular fashion around the tubes. The turns and twists of the tubes are navigated automatically, so this feels more like riding a roller coaster.

The enemies race ahead of you, all of them, at the very beginning, and you can pick up power-ups like shields, turbo, weapons and go after them. But the game doesn't actually allow you to see much of what's going on. I rode around for a while, rarely encountering any opponents. When I found some and shot at them, I did not know if I managed to hit them or not. There's no indicator at all.

There are other obstacles and seemingly random plasma shots being fired at me, and I cannot tell where they are coming from. It's that feeling that you are being shot at, and you are on a roller coaster and thus cannot do anything about it, that really irritates me.

There is a Race Time clock that counts upward in a non-earthly fashion. It counts to 100 seconds before the minute hand ticks up by one. Maybe this is intentional, maybe it's not. If it's intentional, I can't understand it at all.

The Lap Time on the other side of the screen does not seem to work. I was silly enough to use the default 5 laps for my first attempt, and after about 2 laps (?) I ended up bugging out into a black screen with no movement. I could still seemingly accelerate and brake, but I wasn't going anywhere. 

There are obstacles on the course, and if you get stuck behind one, you basically are stuck until you find your way out. I tried a different racer and a different venue second time around, and I got stuck around the same obstacle two laps in a row. I had no idea how I got past it the first time, and I just couldn't the second time. Dare I say, I had seen enough.

[h1]Controls[/h1]
It does have controller support, seems to work fine.

[h1]Graphics and Music[/h1]
Graphics aren't bad, also don't feel very modern either. I understand for a low-budget production, this is decent. The music is meh.

[h1]Pricing[/h1]
The game is asking for $9.99 USD currently in Early Access. This is too much at this stage. Not sure what it will end up being, but its current glitchy nature makes it not exactly something to enjoy. If you want to buy it and help the developers out by trying and testing, while offering constructive criticism so that they can make a better game, then by all means. But that's probably the only reason to buy it right now.

[h1]Positives[/h1]
+Interesting idea ?
+VR support ?

[h1]Negatives[/h1]
-Not exactly a racing game
-I am not sure why it has VR support, because you are scrolling on a predetermined track, essentially
-Race Time (in-game clock) does not work
-Lap Time does not register
-Game randomly bugs out to unplayable states
-Not well optimized
-Difficult to see what's going on half of the time if you are trying to shoot down some enemies
-Priced too high for something in its current state

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
[i]Tubular Rift[/i] is supposed to be a racing game, but it does not feel like one. You have no idea where you are going and you certainly do not know if the race will end. One thing that's consistent is its glitchy nature, and it is likely to cause you to quit rather quickly after starting. Game needs a lot of work and is trying to also tap into the VR aspect, though I cannot imaging what VR support would bring to the table for this game, since you are riding around on rails essentially. Definitely not recommended.

The following is a short gameplay video I created, 2 vehicles, 2 venues, and a lot of glitches later, I had seen enough:

https://youtu.be/sOACu_rhWlY
